## Restart files: write, bundle, read (`outputs: type: restart`, `-r`) {#sec-ch14-restart}

### Summary

The state is saved, not the history. Run-to-date meters (the gravity-work fix total, the positivity meters) start
again from zero after a resume (`gravity_work_fix`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl >}}).

A restart file is the saved simulation state and output schedule from which a run resumes
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}); see @sec-ch01-initialization
for its distinction from a YAML deck and the informal term case.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Saves each block's whole state and output schedule, bundles the parts, and resumes from the bundle.

**Data.** Writes `<basename>.<kkkkk>.restart`; on resume each block reads its own entry and the schedules.

**Placement.** `make_outputs` (write, also on the final call); `_init_from_restart` at initialisation (read).

**Activation.** `outputs: - type: restart` (`dt`); driver argument `-r <file>`. Default: no restart output.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact state in its own dtype; resume needs the same decomposition; meters restart at 0.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-restart-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $t_r$ the time stored in a restart file [s]; $t_\text{next}$ an
output's saved next time [s]; $\Delta t_o$ an output's interval `dt` [s]; $N$ the number of outputs [count].

### Derivation

None for the format. One rule fixes when a restored output fires next. With the saved $t_\text{next}$, the restored
time $t_r$ and the output's current interval $\Delta t_o$:

$$
t_\text{next} \leftarrow
\begin{cases}
t_r + \Delta t_o, & \Delta t_o > 0 \text{ and } t_\text{next} > t_r + \Delta t_o,\\
t_\text{next}, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
t_\text{next}^\text{new} = t_r - (t_r \bmod \Delta t_o) \quad (\Delta t_o > 0).
$$ {#eq-ch14-restart-next}

Why the rule has these two cases, in four steps (`_init_from_restart`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}):

1. *A matched output keeps its saved time if that time is within one interval.* Then it fires on schedule, as it
   would have without the restart.
2. *A saved time more than one interval ahead is clamped to $t_r+\Delta t_o$.* That happens when the interval shrank
   between the runs, or when the output was disabled by a far-future time. Kept, it would delay the output or keep it
   from ever firing.
3. *An interval $\Delta t_o\le0$ keeps the saved time.* There is no grid to clamp to.
4. *An output new in the resumed card joins the grid of multiples of $\Delta t_o$ at or below $t_r$*, so it fires at
   the first output check, and the grid of the new run is the grid of an uninterrupted one. With $\Delta t_o\le0$ it
   starts at $t_r$.

Round-off: the clamp adds two doubles, $t_r+\Delta t_o$, one rounding of at most $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$
relative; the grid point $t_r-\operatorname{fmod}(t_r,\Delta t_o)$ is exact in `fmod` and rounds once in the
subtraction, so it lies within $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}t_r$ of the multiple of $\Delta t_o$. A port of the rule
confirms steps 1 to 3 [check `src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/restart_check.py`, output `restart_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Step 4 is
`[C2]`, and a clamped output writes every $\Delta t_o$ from $t_r+\Delta t_o$ (`[C3]`).

### Numerical method

**Write.** `RestartOutput` forces `combine` on ({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::RestartOutput >}}).
`write_output_file` copies every defined tensor of the block's variable map to the CPU, ghosts included. It drops
`scalar_r` when `scalar_s` and `hydro_u` are both present, because the primitive scalar is rebuilt on read. It adds
`last_time`, `last_cycle`, and per output its `file_number`, `next_time` and two keys (below). The result is saved with
`kintera::save_tensors` to `<basename>.block<r>.<kkkkk>.part`, or `.final.part` on the final write
(`RestartOutput::write_output_file`, {{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::write_output_file >}}). Unlike NetCDF, the restart output also writes on the final
call.

**Keys.** An output's key is a 64-bit FNV-1a hash of its type, its interval and its variable list. The legacy key
hashes the text `type|dt|var...`, with `dt` printed by `std::to_string` (six decimals). The precise key hashes the
type, the eight bytes of `dt` and the variables, separated by zero bytes, so two intervals that print alike still
differ ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::schedule_key_v2 >}}). `output_key` stores the $N$ legacy keys
followed by the $N$ precise keys; a reader that knows only the legacy layout reads the first $N$.

**Bundle.** The last block of the process to write enters `combine_blocks`, which uses the same barrier and
mirror-barrier pattern as NetCDF (@sec-ch14-netcdf). On the root it globs the parts of the frame. One part is renamed
to `<basename>.<kkkkk>.restart`. Several parts are written by `make_restart_bundle` as a text header and the
concatenated payloads, and the parts are deleted ({{< code src/output/combine_restart.cpp make_restart_bundle >}}).
The header is the magic line `SNAPY_RESTART_BUNDLE_V1`, the part count, one `name<TAB>size` line per part, and an
empty line (`kRestartBundleMagic`, {{< code src/output/combine_restart.cpp kRestartBundleMagic >}}).

**Read.** The driver passes the file to `Mesh::initialize`, and each block calls `_init_from_restart`. A relative
path that does not exist is looked up in the output directory. `load_restart` checks for the magic line. In a bundle,
it extracts the part whose name holds `block<r>` for this block's rank, through a temporary file. A file without the
magic is loaded whole (`load_pt_from_bundle`, {{< code src/input/read_restart_file.cpp load_pt_from_bundle >}}). The block then
requires `hydro_u`, `last_time`, `last_cycle`, `file_number` and `next_time`, and resumes at the saved cycle and time
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}).

**Schedules.** Saved slots are matched to the current outputs in three passes
(`claimed`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}):

1. An output whose key equals the key saved in its own position keeps that slot.
2. Each output still unmatched takes the first unclaimed slot with its key.
3. An output still unmatched takes its own position if that slot is unclaimed.

Precise keys are used when `output_key` holds $2N$ entries, legacy keys otherwise. The file number always follows the
position, because the file name is `out<n>`; the next time follows the matched slot and
then @eq-ch14-restart-next. Finally the tensors move to the block's device, and `scalar_r` is rebuilt from `scalar_s` and
`hydro_u` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_init_from_restart >}}).

**Not established:** whether a resume with a changed card works or fails gracefully has not been tested here.

### Code

**A minimal input and resume.** A restart file every 300 s, as in `examples/straka.yaml`:

```yaml
outputs:
  - type: restart
    dt: 300.
```

Resume with `run_hydro -i <card> -r <file>.restart`, where the card is a deck with a `reactions:` block such as
`earth_crm.yaml`, because `run_hydro` builds kintera kinetics from it ({{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}), or
with `straka <card> --restart <file>.restart`. `run_hydro` and
`jupiter_evap_precip_1d` read their arguments with `CommandLine::ParseArguments`, which looks only at two-character
options such as `-r` and skips a longer argument without a message
({{< code src/input/command_line.cpp CommandLine::ParseArguments >}}); so `run_hydro … --restart file` starts a fresh
run. `straka`, `bryan`, `shallow_splash` and `shallow_xy` parse `--restart` themselves and accept both. The
output-entry refusals are those of @sec-ch14-netcdf; `combine` is forced on for this type
({{< code src/output/restart.cpp RestartOutput::RestartOutput >}}). A resume refuses a block entry without
`hydro_u`, `last_time`, `last_cycle`, `file_number` or `next_time` ("missing required variable"), since the block
could not restore its state or schedule.

**The excerpt.** The rule of @eq-ch14-restart-next in `_init_from_restart`:

```cpp
if (dt > 0.0 && saved > current_time + dt) {   // step 2
  output_types[n]->next_time = current_time + dt;
} else {                                        // steps 1 and 3
  output_types[n]->next_time = saved;
}
...                                             // step 4, a new output
next_time = dt > 0.0 ? current_time - std::fmod(current_time, dt) : current_time;
```

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_restart_cycle_limit` | two ranks, straka, restart every 30 s, `nlim: 120`: the run resumed from the first restart file starts at the same cycle as the uninterrupted run at that time, with the same time, $\Delta t$[^rg-007123c4e2b1], mass and energy; both end at cycle 120 and at the same time | $10^{-12}$ abs. (first cycle line); $10^{-9}$ abs. (end time) | printed cycle lines |
| `test_restart_multiblock` | straka with 2, shallow-xy with 4 and shallow-splash with 6 blocks in one process: reloading the restart file gives the same NetCDF frame | exact (`max_abs == 0`) | float NetCDF output |
| this chapter's check, `restart_check.py` | `[C1]`-`[C3]` the resumed next time | exact; grid to round-off | float compare |
| `test_restart_dt_change` | an output whose interval shrank fires on the new grid after a resume | frame-time window | `run_restart_dt_change.py` |
| `test_restart_output_schedule` | appended and inserted output streams keep their schedules and file counters | exact | integer and time compare |
| `test_restart_key_collision` | an interval edited to equal another output's does not renumber that output; legacy and keyless files | exact | integer compare |
| `test_restart_inplace_reorder` | an in-place resume never rewrites a frame the base run completed | exact (md5) | file hashes |
| `test_user_output` `OutputScheduleKey` (precise cadences) | two intervals with the same six-decimal text get different precise keys | exact | integer compare |
| `test_output_barrier` | on return every rank sees the bundled `.restart` file and no `.part` left | exact | file system |

: Tests of restart files; the six runners are registered only on non-Apple builds, and the five single-purpose
ones skip with exit 125 when a tool is missing. `test_user_output` and
`test_output_barrier` carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch14-restart-tests}

`[C1]` of `restart_check.py`: a saved time 600 s or $10^{300}$ ahead is clamped to $t_r+60$ s, one 30 s ahead is
kept, and $\Delta t_o=0$ keeps $10^{300}$. `[C2]`: over 20000 pairs $(t_r,\Delta t_o)$ a new output starts at or below
$t_r$, less than one interval before it, on the grid to $1.8\times10^{-12}$ in units of $\Delta t_o$. `[C3]`: the
clamped output's later writes. `[C20]`–`[C24]` of `derivation_check.py` repeat the cases of steps 1 to 4. The
registered test runs `straka` with `--restart`, which that driver accepts, so the tests do not see the
`run_hydro` difference.[^ch14-restart-chk]

The cycle-limit comparison is `assert_close` with `atol` $10^{-12}$
({{< code tests/run_restart_cycle_limit.py assert_close >}}). The multiblock runner sets
`tlim: 0` and `nlim: 0` and compares with `compare_netcdf`
({{< code tests/run_restart_multiblock.py compare_netcdf >}}). Pass status at the pin was not run
for this chapter.

::: {.callout-important title="Check: what the multiblock test covers"}
`test_restart_multiblock` sets `nlim: 0`, and the integrator stops when the step count reaches `nlim`[^rg-01407341acf5]. So neither leg
takes a step: the test checks that the state at $t = 0$ survives a write, a bundle of 2, 4 or 6 parts and a read, in one
process. It does not compare a resumed run with an uninterrupted one after steps. That comparison is
`test_restart_cycle_limit`, at two ranks with one block each, to $10^{-12}$ on the printed first resumed cycle.
The integrator's stop rule is pyharp's `IntegratorImpl::stop` (not part of snapy): it stops once the step count
reaches a non-negative `nlim` ([`pyharp integrator.cpp:89-99`](https://github.com/chengcli/pyharp/blob/4721715855e937c1e8b218e964c0655f46e56e29/src/integrator/integrator.cpp#L89-L99), `stop`), at the pyharp pin of @sec-ch10-redo.
:::

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A restart must be read with the decomposition that wrote it. In a bundle, a block whose rank has no entry gets
  an empty map and stops with "missing required variable: hydro_u". A single-part file is loaded whole by every
  block, whatever its rank, with no check. That case is read from the code and has not been run.
- Restarts across decompositions are not supported.[^ch14-restart-decomp] The multiblock test varies the blocks per
  process in one process; it does not change the global block count.
- A resumed run rewrites its last outputs, including its source restart file, and the restart index does not
  advance.[^ch14-restart-rewrite]
- Run-to-date meters are not carried across a restart.
- The restart runners launch one or two processes; larger runs are not tested.
:::

[^ch14-restart-decomp]: Requested in chengcli/snapy#138, which is closed.

[^ch14-restart-rewrite]: chengcli/snapy#277, open.
